question:
The Therigatha is a Buddhist text, part of the ___, is a collection of verses composed by bhikkhunis.

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Vinaya Pitaka
Mahavamsa
Dipavamsa
Sutta Pitaka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sutta Pitaka

Explanation:
The Therigatha is an important Buddhist text, which is part of the Sutta Pitaka. It is a collection of verses composed by bhikkhunis (Buddhist nuns) and is included in the Khuddaka Nikaya. This text reflects the experiences, struggles, and spiritual journeys of early Buddhist nuns. The Sutta Pitaka is a collection of Buddha's discourses and teachings, considered one of the three Pitakas (Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka) in Buddhist literature.

Extra Facts:
The Therigatha, also known as 'Verses of the Elder Nuns,' is a significant example of women's spiritual expression in ancient India. It contains around 73 verses by bhikkhunis, showcasing their lives and devotion to the Buddha. This text highlights not only Buddhism but also the role of women in ancient Indian literature.

question_hi:
थेरिगाथा एक बौद्ध ग्रंथ है, जो ___ का हिस्सा है, भिक्षुणियों द्वारा रचित छंदों का एक संग्रह है।

[NTPC CBT 2]
options_hi: विनय पिटक
महावम्सा
दीपवमसा
सुत्त पिटक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सुत्त पिटक

Explanation:
थेरिगाथा बौद्ध साहित्य का एक महत्वपूर्ण ग्रंथ है, जो सुत्त पिटक का हिस्सा है। यह भिक्षुणियों द्वारा रचित छंदों का संग्रह है और खुद्दक निकाय में शामिल है। यह ग्रंथ प्रारंभिक बौद्ध भिक्षुणियों के अनुभवों, संघर्षों और आध्यात्मिक यात्रा को दर्शाता है। सुत्त पिटक बुद्ध के उपदेशों और धम्म से संबंधित ग्रंथों का संग्रह है, जिसे तीन पिटकों (विनय पिटक, सुत्त पिटक, अभिधम्म पिटक) में से एक माना जाता है।

Extra Facts:
थेरिगाथा को 'भिक्षुणियों के गीत' के रूप में भी जाना जाता है और यह प्राचीन भारत में महिलाओं की आध्यात्मिक अभिव्यक्ति का एक महत्वपूर्ण उदाहरण है। इसमें लगभग 73 भिक्षुणियों के छंद शामिल हैं, जो उनके जीवन और बुद्ध के प्रति भक्ति को दर्शाते हैं। यह ग्रंथ न केवल बौद्ध धर्म बल्कि प्राचीन भारतीय साहित्य में महिलाओं की भूमिका को भी उजागर करता है।

question:
Buddha delivered his first sermon which is called_______, at Sarnath to his five disciples.

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Niranjana
Mahabhinishkramana
Maha parinirvana
Dharmachakra pravartana
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dharmachakra pravartana

Explanation:
Dharmachakra pravartana refers to Buddha's first sermon, which he delivered at Sarnath to his five disciples (Panchavargiya Bhikkhus). This event is highly significant in Buddhist history as it marked the foundation of Buddhism. In this sermon, Buddha preached the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path, setting the wheel of Dharma (Dhamma) in motion. Hence, it is called 'Dharmachakra Pravartana' (Turning the Wheel of Dharma).

Extra Facts:
Sarnath (near Varanasi) is one of the most sacred Buddhist pilgrimage sites. Emperor Ashoka later built stupas and pillars here, which are excellent examples of Buddhist art. The Dhamek Stupa, constructed during the Gupta period, is a prominent structure in Sarnath.

question_hi:
बुद्ध ने अपना पहला उपदेश सारनाथ में अपने पांच शिष्यों को दिया था, जिसे _______ कहा जाता है।

[NTPC CBT 2]
options_hi: निरंजना
महाभिनिष्क्रमण
महा परिनिर्वाण
धर्मचक्र प्रवर्तन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है धर्मचक्र प्रवर्तन

Explanation:
धर्मचक्र प्रवर्तन बुद्ध द्वारा दिए गए पहले उपदेश को कहा जाता है, जिसे उन्होंने सारनाथ में अपने पांच शिष्यों (पंचवर्गीय भिक्षुओं) को दिया था। यह घटना बौद्ध धर्म के इतिहास में अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि इसमें बुद्ध ने चार आर्य सत्य और अष्टांगिक मार्ग का उपदेश दिया। इसी उपदेश से बौद्ध धर्म की नींव पड़ी और इसे 'धर्मचक्र प्रवर्तन' (धर्म के पहिए को गति देने) के रूप में जाना जाता है।

Extra Facts:
सारनाथ (वाराणसी के निकट) बौद्ध धर्म के प्रमुख तीर्थ स्थलों में से एक है। यहीं पर बुद्ध ने अपना पहला उपदेश दिया था। बाद में सम्राट अशोक ने यहां स्तूप और स्तंभ बनवाए, जो बौद्ध कला के उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण हैं। धमेक स्तूप सारनाथ की प्रमुख संरचना है, जिसका निर्माण गुप्त काल में हुआ था।

question:
The Shailendra kings who founded their empire in South-east Asia in the 8th Century AD were the followers of__________

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Buddhism
Shaivism
Jainism
Hinduism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Buddhism

Explanation:
In the 8th Century AD, the Shailendra dynasty established their empire in Southeast Asia (present-day Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand). These kings were followers of Mahayana Buddhism. They constructed grand monuments like Borobudur (the world's largest Buddhist temple), which reflects the influence of Buddhism. Although some Shailendra rulers also patronized Hinduism (particularly Shaivism), their primary religious identity was associated with Buddhism.

Extra Facts:
The Shailendra dynasty is considered a golden era for the spread of Indian culture in Southeast Asia. They not only promoted Buddhism but also encouraged Sanskrit literature, art, and architecture. The Borobudur Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and an excellent example of Mahayana Buddhist sculpture and architecture.

question_hi:
8वीं सदी ईस्वी में दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया में अपने साम्राज्य की स्थापना करने वाले शैलेंद्र राजा किस धर्म के अनुयायी थे?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: बौद्ध धर्म
शैव धर्म
जैन धर्म
हिन्दू धर्म
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है बौद्ध धर्म

Explanation:
8वीं सदी ईस्वी में शैलेंद्र राजवंश ने दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया (वर्तमान इंडोनेशिया, मलेशिया, थाईलैंड) में अपना साम्राज्य स्थापित किया था। ये राजा महायान बौद्ध धर्म के अनुयायी थे। इन्होंने बोरोबुदुर (विश्व का सबसे बड़ा बौद्ध मंदिर) जैसे भव्य स्मारकों का निर्माण करवाया, जो बौद्ध धर्म के प्रभाव को दर्शाता है। हालाँकि, कुछ शैलेंद्र शासकों ने हिंदू धर्म (विशेषकर शैव धर्म) को भी संरक्षण दिया, लेकिन उनकी मुख्य धार्मिक पहचान बौद्ध धर्म से जुड़ी थी।

Extra Facts:
शैलेंद्र राजवंश का शासनकाल दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया में भारतीय संस्कृति के प्रसार का स्वर्णिम काल माना जाता है। इन्होंने न केवल बौद्ध धर्म को बढ़ावा दिया बल्कि संस्कृत साहित्य, कला और वास्तुकला को भी प्रोत्साहित किया। बोरोबुदुर मंदिर यूनेस्को की विश्व धरोहर स्थल है और यह बौद्ध धर्म के महायान संप्रदाय की मूर्तिकला एवं स्थापत्य कला का उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है।

question:
Which of the following structure is associated with Buddhism?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Pallava
Mandapa
Shikhara
Stupa
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Stupa

Explanation:
The Stupa is a significant structure associated with Buddhism. It is a hemispherical or dome-shaped monument that houses relics of the Buddha or other Buddhist saints. Stupas were primarily constructed during the spread of Buddhism and are regarded as symbols of the faith. Famous stupas include the Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh) and the Amaravati Stupa (Andhra Pradesh), built during the Mauryan period and later dynasties.

Extra Facts:
The design of a Stupa reflects Buddhist philosophy, where the dome symbolizes the sky, representing Nirvana. Emperor Ashoka commissioned numerous stupas to propagate Buddhism. Stupas often feature Toranas (gateways) and Vedikas (railings) adorned with Jataka tales.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी संरचना बौद्ध धर्म से संबंधित है?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: पल्लव
मंडप
शिखर
स्तूप
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है स्तूप

Explanation:
स्तूप बौद्ध धर्म से संबंधित एक महत्वपूर्ण संरचना है। यह एक गोलाकार या अर्धगोलाकार ढांचा होता है, जिसमें बुद्ध या अन्य बौद्ध संतों के अवशेष रखे जाते थे। स्तूपों का निर्माण मुख्य रूप से बौद्ध धर्म के प्रसार के दौरान किया गया था और ये बौद्ध धर्म के प्रतीक के रूप में जाने जाते हैं। प्रसिद्ध स्तूपों में साँची स्तूप (मध्य प्रदेश) और अमरावती स्तूप (आंध्र प्रदेश) शामिल हैं। इनका निर्माण मौर्य काल और उसके बाद के शासकों द्वारा करवाया गया था।

Extra Facts:
स्तूप का डिज़ाइन बौद्ध धर्म के दर्शन को दर्शाता है, जहाँ गुंबद आकाश की ओर इशारा करता है, जो मोक्ष का प्रतीक है। सम्राट अशोक ने बौद्ध धर्म के प्रचार के लिए कई स्तूपों का निर्माण करवाया था। स्तूपों के चारों ओर तोरण द्वार और वेदिका बनाई जाती थी, जिन पर बौद्ध जातक कथाओं को उकेरा जाता था।

question:
Which of the following is the largest stupa in India?

[SSC MTS ]
options: Kesariya
Dhamekh
Amaravati
Bharhut
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kesariya

Explanation:
The Kesariya Stupa is the largest stupa in India, located in the Champaran district of Bihar. It stands approximately 104 feet tall and was built during the Gupta period (5th-6th century CE). This stupa is associated with Buddhism and is believed to be the place where Lord Buddha spent his last days before attaining Mahaparinirvana. Its grand architecture and size make it one of the most significant Buddhist monuments in India.

Extra Facts:
The Kesariya Stupa is also known as the 'Great Stupa'. It is believed that Buddha announced his impending Nirvana to his disciples here. The stupa was discovered in the 19th century by British archaeologists. Built with mud bricks, the stupa features Buddhist symbols in its design.

☛ Bharhut Stupa - Located in Madhya Pradesh, related to the Shunga period (2nd century BCE)

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन भारत का सबसे बड़ा स्तूप है?

[SSC MTS ]
options_hi: केसरिया
धमेख
अमरावती
भरहुत
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है केसरिया

Explanation:
केसरिया स्तूप भारत का सबसे बड़ा स्तूप है, जो बिहार के चंपारण जिले में स्थित है। यह स्तूप लगभग 104 फीट ऊँचा है और इसका निर्माण गुप्त काल (5वीं-6वीं शताब्दी) में हुआ था। यह स्तूप बौद्ध धर्म से जुड़ा हुआ है और माना जाता है कि भगवान बुद्ध ने अपने अंतिम दिनों में यहाँ विश्राम किया था। इस स्तूप की वास्तुकला और आकार इसे भारत के सबसे महत्वपूर्ण बौद्ध स्मारकों में से एक बनाता है।

Extra Facts:

question:
In Jainism, the word 'Jain' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jina', which means_________,implying one who has transcended all human passions.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Conqueror
Immortal
Vigour
Candour
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Conqueror

Explanation:
In Jainism, the word 'Jain' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jina', which means Conqueror. It refers to someone who has conquered all inner passions, desires, and emotions. According to Jain philosophy, a 'Jina' or 'Jain' is one who has overcome the bondage of karma and attained liberation (Moksha). Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, is also called 'Jina' because he achieved victory over his senses through self-discipline and asceticism.

Extra Facts:
Jainism is one of the ancient religions of India, originating around the 6th century BCE. It has two major sects: Shwetambara (white-clad monks) and Digambara (sky-clad monks). The core principles of Jainism are based on Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), and Aparigraha (non-possession).

question:
The rules made for the Buddhist "Sangha” were written down in a book called ________ .

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Abhidhamma Pitaka
Sutta pitaka
Vinaya pitaka
Milinda Panha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vinaya Pitaka

Explanation:
The Vinaya Pitaka is one of the three divisions of the Buddhist Tipitaka, containing the rules and disciplinary codes for the monastic community (Sangha). It outlines the daily conduct, ethical guidelines, admission procedures, and disciplinary measures for monks and nuns. This text is also known as the Book of Discipline. It was compiled during the First Buddhist Council (483 BCE) under the leadership of Mahakasyapa. The Vinaya Pitaka is highly regarded in both Theravada and Mahayana traditions.

Extra Facts:
The Tipitaka consists of Sutta Pitaka (Buddha's discourses), Vinaya Pitaka (monastic rules), and Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical analysis). Early Buddhist scriptures were written in Pali. Later texts like Mahavibhasha and Milinda Panha explore advanced Buddhist philosophy.

question:
Who was the twenty-fourth Jain Tirthankara?

Solution: Correct Answer is Mahavira

Explanation:
In Jainism, there are 24 Tirthankaras, and Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara. He was born in 599 BCE in Kundagrama (Vaishali). He is also known as 'Vardhamana' and 'Jina' (the conqueror). Mahavira revived Jain principles and emphasized the five great vows—Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), and Aparigraha (non-possession). He attained Nirvana at the age of 72 in 527 BCE in Pavapuri.

Extra Facts:
Mahavira's father was Siddhartha (a Jnatrika Kshatriya) and mother Trishala (a Lichchhavi princess). His chief disciple was Gautama Swami. Jainism is divided into two sects—Shvetambara and Digambara. Mahavira's teachings are compiled in the Agama literature.

question:

Explanation:

Extra Facts:
The Sanchi Stupa complex includes other historical structures like the Ashoka Pillar, monasteries, and temples. The carvings here depict scenes from the life of Buddha. During the Gupta period (5th century), the stupa was further expanded. Sanchi holds significance as it reflects the influence of both Theravada and Mahayana schools of Buddhism.

In contrast, traders and artisans could more easily adhere to non-violence in their professions.

Extra Facts:
Jainism prescribes the Five Great Vows (Panch Mahavrat), which include Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (chastity), and Aparigraha (non-possession). Monks and ascetics follow these strictly, while laypeople observe them in a more relaxed manner.

question:
Xuan Zang and other pilgrims spent time studying in Nalanda, the most famous Buddhist monastery, located in which of the following Indian state?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Odisha
Bengal
Bihar
Sikkim
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bihar

Explanation:
Nalanda University was a prominent Buddhist learning center in ancient India, located in the present-day state of Bihar. Established during the Gupta Empire in the 5th century, it was later patronized by the rulers of the Pala Dynasty. Xuan Zang, a famous Chinese pilgrim, studied here in the 7th century and documented its glory in his travel accounts. Nalanda was a major hub of Mahayana Buddhism, offering education in philosophy, logic, medicine, and more. The university was destroyed in the 12th century by Bakhtiyar Khilji, reducing it to ruins.

Extra Facts:
The name Nalanda derives from the Sanskrit words 'nalam' (lotus) and 'da' (to give), symbolizing 'the giver of knowledge'. It provided free education and attracted international students. Besides Xuan Zang, another Chinese traveler, I-Tsing, also studied here. Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nalanda's ruins are preserved in Bihar's Nalanda district.

question:
Which of the following terms generally refers to a Buddhist monastery in which Buddhist monks live?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Stupas
Chaitya
Grihas
Viharas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Viharas

Explanation:
The term Viharas refers to Buddhist monasteries where monks lived, meditated, and studied. These monasteries were crucial centers for the spread of Buddhism in ancient India. The word Vihara is derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'dwelling' or 'residence.' Early viharas were natural caves, but later they were constructed using stone. Renowned universities like Nalanda and Vikramshila also evolved from viharas.

Extra Facts:
Viharas held great significance in Buddhism, serving not only as religious sites but also as hubs of education and culture. Emperor Ashoka built several viharas. The Ajanta and Ellora caves are examples of viharas where monks resided and Buddhist art flourished.

question:

Asvaghosha
solution:

Explanation:
Menander (or Milinda) was an Indo-Greek ruler who reigned around 165-130 BCE. He is credited with converting to Buddhism under the influence of the Buddhist monk Nagasena. This event is described in the Buddhist text 'Milindapanha' (Questions of Milinda), which records the philosophical dialogues between Nagasena and Menander. Extra Facts:
The Milindapanha is an important Pali text that provides insights into Theravada Buddhist philosophy. Menander's reign is considered the golden age of the Indo-Greek Kingdom, where Greek and Indian cultures blended. He also contributed to the spread of Buddhism and commissioned stupas.

महावीर और उनके अनुयायियों की शिक्षाओं को लगभग 1500 वर्ष पहले वल्लभी (गुजरात) में लिखा गया था। यह जैन धर्म के आगम साहित्य का संकलन था, जिसे वल्लभी संगीति के नाम से जाना जाता है। यह संगीति 5वीं-6वीं शताब्दी ईस्वी में आयोजित की गई थी और इसमें जैन धर्म के मूल ग्रंथों को व्यवस्थित किया गया था। देवर्धिगणि क्षमाश्रमण इस संगीति के प्रमुख आचार्य थे। यह घटना जैन धर्म के इतिहास में एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ थी, क्योंकि इससे जैन धर्म के सिद्धांतों और शिक्षाओं को संरक्षित किया गया।
